Check and Complete the Arguments of Function Calls

Source: R/all_args_here.R
all_args_here.Rd

Checks that the function calls inside a function are written with all their arguments, and returns the function with the missing arguments added. For instance, base::paste0(letters[1:2]) becomes base::paste0(letters[1:2], collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE).

The calls must already be written with their package (e.g., base::paste0(); run colons_check first), otherwise an error is returned, except the calls not analyzed (see the Details section) and the calls, without package, of the internal functions of x, as defined in colons_check ("INTERNAL_FUNCTION").

Usage

all_args_here(
  x,
  table_export = FALSE,
  fun_export = FALSE,
  out_path = NULL,
  df_name = "res.tsv",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

Function to check, written without quotes and brackets (e.g., fun1 or pkg::fun1).

table_export

Single logical value. Write the table (see the Value section) into the df_name file of out_path, instead of printing it?

fun_export

Single logical value. If TRUE, the corrected function is written into the <name>_safer.R file of out_path instead of being returned (e.g., fun1_safer.R for x = fun1 or x = pkg::fun1), as fun1_safer <- function(...), which base::source() recreates. Nothing is written if nothing has to be corrected, but an error is returned if the file already exists and overwrite is FALSE, or if x is not a function name (e.g., function(x){x} or FUN_LIST$fun).

out_path

Single character string: path of an existing folder where the files are written. Required when table_export or fun_export is TRUE; otherwise not used, but a non-NULL value must still be a single non-empty character string. NULL by default.

df_name

Single character string (not ""): name of the file of the table, written in out_path when table_export is TRUE.

overwrite

Single logical value. Overwrite the files already existing in out_path (df_name and <name>_safer.R) when table_export or fun_export is TRUE?

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

The corrected function, which keeps the environment of x, or NULL, invisibly, if nothing has to be corrected, if fun_export is TRUE, or if x contains no function call, as a primitive function like base::sum (with a warning).

The table of the detected calls is printed as a message, or written into a file if table_export is TRUE, but never returned. Its columns are:

  • $LINE_NB: line number in the code of x (see the Details section).

  • $FUN_NAME: function name.

  • $FUN_ARGS: the call as written, without its package (e.g., sort(v)). "NOT_CONSIDERED" for a name followed by ( inside a string (e.g., "a(" in base::paste0("a(", x)), which is not a call (the calls with a function name written between quotes or after $ or @ are not listed).

  • $FUN_POS: position of the first character of the function name in the line, after removal of the leading and repeated spaces.

  • $DEF_ARGS: arguments of the function with their default values ("" for a function without arguments, e.g., base::Sys.time(), and for "NOT_CONSIDERED" in $FUN_ARGS). "NO_ARGS": primitive function whose arguments are not available (e.g., base::return()); "INTERNAL_FUNCTION": call, written without package, of an internal function inside the function that defines it (see the Description section); "SKIPPED": call not analyzed (see the Details section).

  • $MISSING_ARG_NAMES: names of the missing arguments, and of the arguments written with a partial name.

  • $MISSING_ARGS: these arguments with their proposed values.

  • $STATUS: "GOOD" if all the arguments are written, otherwise the proposed call. "" if the call is not analyzed (see $FUN_ARGS, $DEF_ARGS and the warnings), or if the function has no argument other than ... (e.g., base::Sys.time() or base::c()).

Other messages: "EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN" if no argument is missing, "ARGUMENTS WITH EMPTY VALUE" (empty values inserted into the corrected function, see the Details section) and "CORRECTIONS NOT APPLIED" (proposals not inserted into the corrected function, each with its reason).

Details

Analyzed calls: the names followed by (, except function, if, for, while, repeat, else and the names preceded by $ or @ (e.g., x$fun()). A function passed without brackets (e.g., FUN = base::as.character) or whose name is written between quotes (e.g., base::"rownames<-"(x, "a")) is not checked. The calls inside formulas, one-sided ones included (e.g., offset() in y ~ x + offset(z), or base::mean() in ~ base::mean(.x)), the calls inside quote(), bquote(), expression(), alist() and substitute(), whose arguments are code used as data (e.g., base::paste() in the plotmath label base::expression(base::paste("Temp (", degree, "C)"))), except the code that R evaluates (.() and spliced ..() of bquote(), its where argument, and the env argument of substitute()), the function called by .Internal() (e.g., toupper in base::.Internal(toupper(x))) and as.environment() are not analyzed ("SKIPPED"). The other functions that use the code of their arguments get the completed code (e.g., the default axis label of ggplot2::aes(x = base::log(y)) becomes base::log(x = y, base = base::exp(x = 1))). A call written with more arguments than its function has is not analyzed, with a warning (also for a valid replacement call like base::body(f, envir = e) <- v). The package of each pkg::fun() call must be installed (not only loaded with pkgload::load_all()), and the stats, graphics, grDevices, utils, datasets and methods packages must be attached, as in a default R session, otherwise an error is returned.

Missing arguments: a value written without argument name gets its name (e.g., base::sort(v) becomes base::sort(x = v, decreasing = FALSE)), a partial name is completed (only for the arguments before ..., as in R), and the other missing arguments are added with their default value, written with packages and argument names (e.g., base::log(x = 2) becomes base::log(x = 2, base = base::exp(x = 1))). An empty value (e.g., envir = ), which a function written in R treats as a missing argument (except the first argument of an S3 generic function, which selects the method), is written instead when the default value cannot be copied safely: no default value (e.g., new in base::.libPaths()); a default value that depends on another argument, on a variable internal to the called function, on the frame where it is evaluated (e.g., parent.frame(), a formula or a function definition), or on an object that x does not find, or finds differently (e.g., an internal function of a package, or a variable masked by an argument of x); a default value whose function calls are written pkg::fun(), lack some arguments (e.g., getOption("digits")) or use the code of their arguments (e.g., quote(exp(1))); an argument tested with missing() (e.g., nrow in base::matrix(x, ncol = 2)). An argument already written with an empty value is accepted, except if its default value can be copied, which is then added.

Corrected function: the missing arguments are inserted into the code of x, whose line breaks are kept. A proposal is not inserted, and is listed with its reason in the "CORRECTIONS NOT APPLIED" message, when the call receives a value from a pipe (|>, %>%, %<>%, %T>% or %!>%), forwards ..., has an empty argument (e.g., base::sum(1, )), is the target of an assignment (e.g., base::rownames(x) <- "a"), or has a value written without name that is also proposed with its name; when the called function counts its arguments with nargs() (e.g., base::diag()), or is a builtin primitive that would receive an empty value (e.g., PACKAGE = in base::.Call()); when the called function is an S3 generic whose first argument is not written, or is written without name while a method names it differently (e.g., formula in t.test.formula()), or when a method has neither ... nor an added argument (e.g., digits for round.POSIXt()), or has arguments that an added argument matches partially (e.g., y matching ylim and ylab of plot.table()); and when the call cannot be read, located, parsed or matched to its $STATUS proposal.

An error is returned if x contains \(x) lambda functions (only detected with source references): run lambda_check first.

Source references: line 1 is the line of the function keyword. Comments and indentation are kept only if x carries its source references (attribute srcref). Functions created with options(keep.source = FALSE) (default of Rscript) and functions of installed packages (e.g., saferDev::colons_check) have none: their deparsed code is analyzed, without comments and with line numbers that differ from the source file.

Limitations: the detection is text-based, and some unusual writings (e.g., in comments) can dupe it. The $STATUS proposals remain suggestions to check. Please report unexpected results here.

See also

The code checkers of saferDev, in the recommended order of use: super_assign_check, lambda_check, colons_check, all_args_here, curly_bracket_check, true_false_check, for_loop_nb_check (see vignette("saferDev")).

Examples

# Without source references ("Run examples" link, Rscript), line numbers and comments differ.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/all_args_here.html
fun1 <- function(x){
    base::paste0(x, "a") # collapse and recycle0 arguments not written
}
fun1_safer <- saferDev::all_args_here(x = fun1, table_export = FALSE, fun_export = FALSE,
    out_path = NULL, df_name = "res.tsv", overwrite = FALSE, safer_check = FALSE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # arguments added
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), ARGUMENTS ARE MISSING.
#> 
#>   LINE_NB FUN_NAME       FUN_ARGS FUN_POS
#> 1       3   paste0 paste0(x, "a")       7
#>                                 DEF_ARGS  MISSING_ARG_NAMES
#> 1 ..., collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE collapse, recycle0
#>                        MISSING_ARGS
#> 1 collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE
#>                                              STATUS
#> 1 paste0(x, "a", collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE)
#> 
fun1_safer # corrected function
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     base::paste0(x, "a", collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE)
#> }
#> <environment: 0x6235be69cd08>
# Write the table (res.tsv) and the corrected function (fun1_safer.R) in a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(check = FALSE), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::all_args_here(x = fun1, table_export = TRUE, fun_export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir,
    df_name = "res.tsv", overwrite = FALSE, safer_check = FALSE, lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = "")
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), ARGUMENTS ARE MISSING.
#> RESULT EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpQNRq2A/dir11043b5dd324/res.tsv
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpQNRq2A/dir11043b5dd324/fun1_safer.R
#> 
base::unlink(x = tempo_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = FALSE, expand = TRUE) # folder removed
